answer: The forge multiplier is published, charged in kernel, and ember lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 930 identities would post 3784 proofs and burn roughly 41 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
